'''''Orchis italica''''', the '''naked man orchid''' or the '''Italian orchid''', is a species of [[orchid]] native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]].<ref name = qfarms>{{cite web|last=Q Farms|title=''Orchis italica'' or The Naked man orchid|url=http://pakagri.blogspot.com/2012/07/orchis-italica-or-naked-man-orchid.html|work=Farming & Agriculture|accessdate=6 September 2012|date=28 July 2012|archive-date=7 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120807221727/http://pakagri.blogspot.com/2012/07/orchis-italica-or-naked-man-orchid.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  It gets its common name from the lobed lip (labellum) of each flower which resembles the general shape of a naked [[man]] wearing a hat. In Italy, it was believed that the consumption of the plant is conducive to [[virility]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |magazine=[[National Geographic]] |issue=December 2019 |title=In Orchids, myth and folk medicine meet}}</ref> It prefers partial shade and low nutrient soil, and flowers in April. ''Orchis italica'' grows up to {{convert|50|cm|in}} in height, with bright pink, densely clustered flowers.

==Distribution==
''Orchis italica'' is commonly found in large clusters in the Mediterranean region.<ref name = first>{{cite web | url= http://www.first-nature.com/flowers/orchis-italica.php| title=''Orchis italica'' – Naked man orchid, Italian orchid |website=First Nature |accessdate=31 December 2016 }}</ref> It is native to southwestern Europe ([[Balearic Islands]], [[Portugal]], [[Sardinia]], and [[Spain]]), southeastern Europe ([[Albania]], [[Greece]], [[Italy]], [[Crete]], [[Sicily]], and countries of the former [[Yugoslavia]]), western Asia ([[Cyprus]], the East [[Aegean Islands]], [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]], [[Israel]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=דנין |first1=אבינעם |last2=אורי |first2=פרגמן–ספיר |title=סחלב איטלקי |url=https://flora.org.il/plants/orcita/ |website=צמחיית ישראל וסביבתה |publisher=הגן הבוטני הישראלי ירושלים |access-date=28 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621151704/https://flora.org.il/plants/ORCITA |archive-date=21 June 2021 |language=Hebrew |url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Turkey]]), and northern Africa ([[Algeria]], [[Libya]], [[Morocco]], and [[Tunisia]]).<ref name=WCSP>{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=142690 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191221154851/https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=142690 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 21, 2019 |title=''Orchis italica'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref>
